newsitem.title: EGYPT: French-dominated bank in Egypt ups profi.
newsitem.headline: French-dominated bank in Egypt ups profi.

text.p: National Societe Generale Bank made net after-tax profits of 56.98 million pounds ($16.79 million) in calendar 1996, 18 percent up on 48.39 million in 1995, the financial weekly al-Borsa said on Sunday.
The profits are equivalent to 56.98 pounds for each of the one million shares, which traded in the range 1,000 to 1,100 pounds a share on the Egyptian stock exchange on Sunday.

National Societe Generale is 51 percent owned by Societe Generale of France. State-run National Bank of Egypt, which was once the majority shareholder, holds 18 percent and the rest of the shares are traded on the stock exchange.
Al-Borsa said the profits were audited but had yet to be endorsed by the annual general meeting of shareholders, who will meet in Cairo on Wednesday.
The board is proposing to increase the bank's capital to 120 million pounds from 100 million by issuing one free share for each five, bank officials said in February.
